cells.cell: Benchmarks Game mandelbrot, all Viv engines
cells.why: The output is a binary PBM (bytes 0-255). Viv writes UTF-8 text only (`print`, `write_text`), so no Viv program can produce the benchmark's bytes.

cells.cell: Benchmarks Game binary-trees, all Viv engines
cells.why: The benchmark allocates recursive tree nodes. Viv forbids recursive record types and has no pointers or references; a tree kept in a preallocated array is a custom memory pool, which the Benchmarks Game rules for this benchmark do not accept.

cells.cell: Benchmarks Game pidigits, all Viv engines
cells.why: Needs arbitrary-precision integers. Viv's only number is a 64-bit float.
The Benchmarks Game has no Numba programs; none were written.
No published Julia version of these kernels was found (searched the suite's repository and the web); none was written for this study.

Refused by py2viv (strict), each at a construct inside the kernel: `np.bitwise_and` (check_mask), the sum of a complex array (cma_pt), `.var(ddof=)` (cronbach), `dtype=np.float32` (grayscott), a default argument that is a function (local_maxima), `np.average` (lstsqr), `dtype=E.dtype` (make_decision), real array times a complex number (mandelbrot), a real value added to a complex array (normalize_complex_arr), `np.tile` (periodic_dist), `np.repeat` (repeating), a row view that the code writes into (wave).

Numba's nopython mode rejects the kernel as the suite's harness decorates it (np-bench reports these as "unsupported" too): check_mask, cronbach, evolve, grouping, local_maxima, make_decision, mandelbrot, periodic_dist.
